title: Compline
hookLine: the night office: keep me as the apple of your eye (Psalm 17:8)
tomorrow: how did Jesus sleep through a storm?

cards: The last thing at night can easily be a screen in the dark: one more video, one more scroll, one more look at tomorrow's calendar.
In a monastery, the last thing is a prayer called Compline, and the Rule of Saint Benedict asks for something unusual after it. Nobody speaks. Not a joke on the stairs, not a reminder about tomorrow.
The night is kept in silence.

teach.b: Compline is the night office, the final prayers in the church's daily round. Catholics pray it as Night Prayer; Anglicans and others keep the old name.
Its psalms differ from book to book, but in some forms one verse returns as a call and answer, from Psalm seventeen: “Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings.”
The apple of the eye is the pupil, the small dark center the eyelid shuts over before you even think. It's guarded by reflex. So the prayer asks to be kept that close all night.
Moses sings the same picture in Deuteronomy: God found his people in a waste howling wilderness, and “he kept him as the apple of his eye.” Here's where it meets a life.
Nights are when a day's worries get loud: a test, a bill, someone you love who's sick. Compline doesn't fix any of them.
It names them, hands them over, and then goes quiet.
Some Christians pray it alone in bed, some with family, some by listening to a choir sing it. The shape stays the same: speak, entrust, then silence.

how: Monks and nuns pray Compline as the day's last office, and some parishes and cathedrals hold sung Compline in the evening; others pray a short form at home before bed.

o: the church's last prayer of the day, at night
a vow of silence taken by monks for life
the final hymn sung at the end of a funeral

games.q: the night prayer — tap the pairs.

s: it's the night office, the last prayers of the day.
the apple of the eye means the pupil
the small dark center the eyelid guards.
you have to know the words perfectly to pray it

games.q: your little sister is scared of the dark and asks what grown-ups say to God at bedtime. what could you tell her from Compline?
o: a list of everything that could go wrong tonight, just to be safe.
keep me as the apple of the eye: asking to be kept close all night.
nothing; night prayers only make people more worried.
games.why: Compline borrows Psalm 17: keep me as the apple of the eye; hide me under the shadow of thy wings. then quiet.

practice: Close your eyes as if the day were already over. If you pray, say the verse slowly, once on the in-breath and once on the out: keep me as the apple of the eye; hide me under the shadow of thy wings.
If you don't, keep the monastery's rule instead: no words at all, aloud or inside, for the rest of the sit.

wordCard.voice: Compline. The church's night prayer, the last of the day: it asks to be kept close, and then falls silent.

orig.note: the Hebrew word in Psalm 17:8 for the apple, the pupil, of the eye.

carryVoice: Your line: the apple of his eye. Kept close, all night long. Then, silence until morning.
